core_obligations: Equivalence of the first two conditions (proof lines 1610-1616): by definition a point has codimension zero exactly when the dimension of its local ring is zero.

Equivalence of (1) and (3), one direction (proof lines 1616-1636): reduce to X quasi-compact and use the filtration of a quasi-separated decent space by open subspaces with bijective maps from quasi-compact schemes; if x lies in U_i but not in the next piece, it is the image of a unique point y of V_i, which is a generic point of an irreducible component when x has codimension zero; since the preimage of the smaller open is a quasi-compact open not containing y, a standard open neighbourhood W of y inside V_i is disjoint from it, and the restriction of the map to W is an isomorphism onto its image, so x is a generic point of the space.

Equivalence of (1) and (3), converse and conclusion (proof lines 1636-1646): if x is a generic point then the map from the closure of y onto the irreducible component of the relevant open subspace is bijective over that component, so the closure of y is an irreducible component and x has codimension zero; the existence of an open subscheme neighbourhood of x then follows from the proposition on dense open subspaces of locally quasi-separated spaces.
proof_roadmap: Identify codimension zero with the local ring having dimension zero by definition.
Reduce to the quasi-compact case and use the filtration by open subspaces with bijective scheme charts to compare generic points.
Quote the proposition on open dense subschemes for the final statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a point of a quasi-separated algebraic space the conditions of having codimension zero, of having zero dimensional local ring and of being a generic point of an irreducible component are equivalent, and that such a point has an open neighbourhood which is a scheme (statement lines 1597-1608). The proof (proof lines 1610-1653) identifies the first two conditions by definition, gives an elementary proof of the equivalence with the third through a filtration by open subspaces with bijective scheme charts, and quotes the proposition on open dense subschemes for the final assertion. H2: an equivalence with an explicit elementary argument, written out in full.
